title: 1999 AHSME Problem 23
statement: The equiangular convex hexagon \(ABCDEF\) has \(AB = 1,\) \(BC = 4,\) \(CD = 2,\) and \(DE = 4.\) The area of the hexagon is

solutions.text:
Each interior angle is \(120^\circ,\) so extending sides \(FA\) and \(BC,\) \(BC\) and \(DE,\) and \(DE\) and \(FA\) cuts off three equilateral corner triangles and forms a large equilateral triangle.

Let \(EF=e\) and \(FA=f.\) Resolving the six sides in directions separated by \(60^\circ\) gives \(f-e=4\) and \(e+f=6,\) so \(e=1\) and \(f=5.\) The corner triangles built on \(AB, CD,\) and \(EF\) are therefore equilateral. The large triangle has side \(1+4+2=7,\) while the removed triangles have sides \(1,2,\) and \(1.\) The area is \[ \begin{aligned} &\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\left(7^2 - 1^2 - 2^2 - 1^2\right) \\ &\quad = \frac{43\sqrt3}{4}. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Extend alternate sides to enclose the hexagon in a large equilateral triangle
Subtract three small equilateral corner triangles from the large one
